body:
When cuobjdump prints an FSEL immediate as `-QNAN`, the text lifter currently emits that display label verbatim, for example `selp.b32 %r5, 0, -QNAN, %p0;`. NVIDIA ptxas rejects this PTX with an unknown symbol and illegal unary minus.

The spelling also loses the NaN payload: independently assembling `0xffffffff` and `0xffc00000` produces distinct FSEL encodings that both disassemble as `-QNAN`. Replacing the label with a canonical NaN would change the selected bits.

This change recovers the encoded 32-bit immediate for the confirmed FSEL immediate form and emits a `.b32` hexadecimal operand. It checks the source position, instruction encoding and negative quiet-NaN bits; missing or conflicting encoding produces an unsupported diagnostic. Other FSEL operands retain their existing handling. A regression test covers both payloads and missing encoding.

Validation on sm_120 with CUDA 13.1 ptxas/cuobjdump:

- Unmodified pinned source reproduced the invalid symbol through a direct `lift_sass_text_to_ptx` call. The patched function preserved both exact payloads and diagnosed missing encoding.
- A complete 1,984-instruction kernel that previously failed at the generated `-QNAN` operand assembled successfully after this change.
- The standalone unit-test target could not compile existing tests that refer to `ptx_parser`, which is absent from the isolated build. The added unit test is therefore not reported as executed; the same cases passed in the direct-library regression executable. Full workspace tests were not run because the checkout's required LLVM dependency is unavailable.

This validates the specific conversion and offline assembly fix. GPU execution and whole-kernel output equivalence have not been tested. The extraction is limited to the confirmed immediate encoding; this PR does not claim general support for every FSEL/NaN encoding.

title: Fix encoded negative qNaN payloads in FSEL recovery
